name: R2-10 acceptance / interpretation rules (frozen before results)
principle: No arbitrary PASS threshold is defined merely to force a positive result. Negative results are valid and must not be reframed as positive.

interpretation_categories.label: NO_USEFUL_CAUSAL_SIGNAL
interpretation_categories.definition: No causal_runtime_candidate family's DEV primary_selection_statistic (h=1 recall@k) exceeds BOTH trivial baselines (global_frequency and last_observation) by an amount distinguishable from DEV-to-DEV cell variance (reported, not a fabricated numeric cutoff). Shuffled_null is reported alongside as the chance/marginal-structure reference.

interpretation_categories.label: MEASURABLE_IMPROVEMENT_INSUFFICIENT_FOR_RETENTION
interpretation_categories.definition: At least one causal_runtime_candidate measurably exceeds both trivial baselines on DEV h=1 recall@k, but R2-10 Phase 0/DEV-tournament evidence alone does not establish whether this translates into a retention benefit (miss-byte reduction) -- that question is explicitly reserved for R2-11 and is NOT answered by R2-10.

interpretation_categories.label: STRONG_CAUSAL_PREDICTION_JUSTIFYING_R2_11
interpretation_categories.definition: Category B holds AND the margin over trivial baselines is large and consistent across all 8 DEV cells (not driven by one workload), making a retention-integration experiment (R2-11) scientifically motivated. Category C is a recommendation to proceed to R2-11 planning, NOT a retention result and NOT a runtime-speedup claim.

forbidden_claims_from_r2_10: runtime speedup / tokens-per-second / latency change -- requires R2-12
generalization beyond the 8 DEV cells (EVAL remains locked)
O_B = O* or any strengthening of AUDIT-ORACLE-001 CASE C semantics

leakage_audit.method: Construct a synthetic trace T and a second synthetic trace T' identical to T up to and including iterator position i, but with every same-layer entry at iterator position > i deliberately altered (different expert sets). For every predictor family exercised in Phase 0, the prediction made at position i for ANY horizon h must be bit-identical between a run against T and a run against T' when only entries <= i are supplied as causal state. tests/test_r2_10_leakage.py implements this for causal_walk.py directly (the single path all predictors consume) plus for every Phase-0-implemented family.
leakage_audit.additional_check: A second synthetic-trace variant alters ONLY layers > l of the same step t (same-step future layers) while leaving layers <= l and all other steps identical; predictions for layer l at that step must again be unaffected -- this specifically exercises the same_step_later_layer forbidden boundary distinct from the same_layer_future boundary.

determinism_audit.method: Same trace + same predictor config + same horizon run twice must yield bit-identical predictions and metrics for every Phase-0-implemented family. No predictor in predictor_space.json uses unseeded randomness; none currently uses randomness at all.
